findings.title: Minor phrasing clunkiness regarding patient stickers
findings.body: The phrase "leave a sticker in the M&M folder on Mr Okafor's notes" is slightly ambiguous. In NHS practice, you typically take a patient demographic label (a "sticker") and put it in the designated folder/book. The current phrasing makes it sound like the folder is physically on the notes, or the sticker goes on the notes inside the folder.
findings.recommendation: Change to "put one of Mr Okafor's stickers in the M&M folder" or "leave one of Mr Okafor's stickers in the M&M folder" for maximum authenticity and clarity.

overall_take: The patch perfectly captures the NHS M&M and safeguarding workflow distinction. Akin's voice remains dry, direct, and observant without becoming didactic. The subtle motivation to 'be in the room' is an excellent narrative touch. Just a minor phrasing suggestion for the sticker action to make it sound exactly like ward slang.
